chunks: He asked about khayrī oil and violet oil: "May I anoint myself with it when we intend to enter iḥrām?" He said: "Yes."
And he asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bath) in al-Madīnah for his iḥrām, so he said: "That suffices him instead of the ghusl at Dhī al-Ḥulayfah."

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state or intention of iḥrām
key_terms.الْخَيْرِيِّ: khayrī oil, a scented oil mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.دُهْنِ: oil used for anointing the body
key_terms.ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhī al-Ḥulayfah, the miqāt near al-Madīnah
key_terms.نُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use oil before entering iḥrām, and does ghusl in al-Madīnah suffice for iḥrām?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings related to preparing for iḥrām. It permits using khayrī and violet oil before entering iḥrām, and it states that ghusl (ritual bath) performed in al-Madīnah for iḥrām is sufficient and does not need to be repeated at Dhī al-Ḥulayfah.
